summary: @servicetitan/suppress-warnings preinstall drops Bun runtime to execute obfuscated payload
details: The package advertises itself as a small React warning-suppression utility but ships a preinstall hook (`node setup.mjs` in package.json) that downloads the Bun runtime from `https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v<ver>/<arch>.zip`, chmod +x's it, and invokes it via `execFileSync` against a bundled 727KB file `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is a single-line obfuscator.io-style payload with a rotating string-array cipher (`WV8StW` shift over the `n7gIxM` array) and mangled identifiers; its behavior is not readable from source and is unrelated to the small plain-JS warning-suppression code in `dist/`. Fetching an alien runtime at install time to execute a heavily obfuscated bundled blob is an install-time RCE / alternate-runtime dropper pattern — it evades scanners that only inspect Node-reachable code and yields arbitrary code execution on every machine that runs `npm install`. The `@servicetitan`-scoped name combined with an implausibly high version number (38.1.5) for a trivial helper is consistent with a dependency-confusion / scope-impersonation attack targeting ServiceTitan build environments.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
